analysis: The closest option develops mainstream business through accounting, finance, economics, marketing, negotiation, strategy, law and organisational behaviour. Quantitative and qualitative methods complement that business core. Rescheduled AI and consumer product design into offered terms.

The analytics option develops programming, databases, statistical learning, economics and modelling, alongside business, strategy and organisational behaviour. Optimisation and Econometrics replace general psychology and marketing to strengthen decision methods. The option gives foundations for operational analysis without claiming inventory, logistics or a full supply-chain sequence.

The responsible enterprise option connects design, accounting, law, strategy and leadership with environmental and governance evidence. Life-cycle analysis, sustainable farming, resource recovery and energy design provide distinct applied decisions about production and innovation. Sustainability foundations and business gateway prerequisites are met, with climate change before renewable-system design.

Kept supported partial alignments in accounting, marketing, investments, organisational behaviour, strategy, law, economics, statistics, programming, information systems and sustainability. The internship choice and required thesis stay separate; optional UCR research is outside the six-term 180 EC schedules.

DISMATH211.name: Linear Algebra

DISMATH314.name: Probability & Statistics

ENSSUST111.name: Climate Change

ENSSUST311.name: Renewable System Design

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: Develops ethically grounded qualitative research design, data collection, analysis and communication.

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication

alignment.rationale: Both introduce financial reporting and accounting analysis. UCR also introduces management accounting and investment appraisal.
Both study marketing decisions and customer needs. UCR emphasises engagement and brand strategy.
Both analyse and plan organisational strategy. UCR focuses on digital transformation.
Both study legal frameworks for businesses. Tilburg focuses on Dutch company law and UCR on cross-border transactions.
Both examine how people, teams and institutions shape organisational behaviour. UCR adds an emphasis on leadership.
Both analyse investments and financial markets. UCR also studies banking and financial institutions.
Both use calculus and optimisation. UCR applies mathematical tools in a broader scientific setting.
Both use R to work with data. Tilburg includes spreadsheet methods and business applications.
Both introduce microeconomic and macroeconomic ideas. Tilburg applies them to business decisions.
Both study aspects of organising information. UCR focuses on database design and queries.
Both use regression and statistical inference. UCR develops econometric methods for causal and predictive questions.
Both develop ethical reasoning. Tilburg applies it specifically to organisations and business decisions.
Both evaluate how organisations create value while managing environmental effects. UCR focuses on product and service life cycles.
Both develop research design and empirical reasoning. Tilburg applies these methods to business management.
